title: Lesson 23 - Consolidating/leveraging multiple Salesforce instances: org consolidation, org-to-org integration, Data Pipelines/Data Connect
description: Given a customer scenario, recommend a design to effectively consolidate and/or leverage data from multiple Salesforce instances, including org consolidation strategies, org-to-org integration, and Data Pipelines/Data Connect.

questions.question: A company has three regional orgs; EU data must stay in the EU instance but a global customer view is required. What design best fits?
options: Integrate/stitch the orgs with a shared global customer key and residency-respecting sync
Use Big Objects to merge the orgs
questions.explanation: Residency forces a multi-org design; a shared global key plus controlled sync gives the unified view without violating residency. Consolidation (A) breaks residency and the others do not achieve the goal.

questions.question: Which TWO are drivers for org CONSOLIDATION rather than integration?
options: A single customer view and shared processes
Data residency requirements that mandate separate instances
Reduced integration complexity and admin/license overhead
Divergent, conflicting business processes per unit
questions.explanation: Shared processes/single view (A) and reduced complexity/overhead (C) favor consolidation; residency (B) and divergent processes (D) favor staying separate/integrated.

questions.question: During an org consolidation, downstream systems break because record IDs changed. What should have prevented this?
options: Using external IDs/cross-references to relink records and keep downstream links valid
questions.explanation: Because Salesforce IDs are org-specific, a consolidation requires external IDs/cross-references to relink and re-key downstream systems; the other options do not preserve identity across orgs.
